projects.heading: Featured Projects
projects.subtitle: A selection of high-impact digital solutions, developed with a focus on scalability and performance.

1.name: Personal Portfolio
1.description: Modern, responsive personal portfolio with bilingual support (EN/PT), dark theme, smooth animations, and a secure contact form powered by EmailJS and reCAPTCHA v3.
1.highlight_1: Custom i18n system using React Context API — bilingual EN/PT support with no external libraries.
1.highlight_2: Dark theme built with CSS custom properties and Tailwind CSS for consistent, maintainable styling.
1.highlight_3: Contact form with server-side EmailJS integration and reCAPTCHA v3 to block spam submissions.
1.challenge_1: Implementing nested dot-notation key resolution for the i18n system without the overhead of libraries like next-intl.
1.challenge_2: Achieving high Lighthouse scores through lazy loading, font preloading, and animation optimization.

2.name: Transparência BR API
2.description: Async REST API built with FastAPI that exposes four datasets from Brazil's Federal Transparency Portal (CGU) — corporate card spending, official travel, contracts and public bids — through versioned /v1/ endpoints. Every page fetched is normalized and stored in PostgreSQL, and stored records can be filtered by agency, period and value range.
2.highlight_1: Explicit layers (api, services, clients, schemas, models, core): business logic depends neither on FastAPI nor on the external API's format.
2.highlight_2: pytest suite covering all four resources, with the Portal mocked via pytest-httpx so tests don't depend on the source being available, running on GitHub Actions on every push.
2.highlight_3: httpx client with retry on 429 and explicit timeouts, custom exceptions with centralized handling, and a /health endpoint.
2.challenge_1: Keeping the integration stable under the Transparency Portal's rate limit, turning third-party failures into predictable API responses instead of stack traces.
2.challenge_2: Normalizing heterogeneous Portal data — dates in two formats and values as Brazilian-formatted text — into DATE and NUMERIC, with a migration that converts existing data losslessly and background writes that keep the API up if the database goes down.

3.name: Local-LLM Email Triage Agent
3.description: Agent that sorts incoming email into 8 semantic categories with an LLM running locally (Ollama + llama3.1), orchestrated by self-hosted n8n on Docker Compose. Prompt, categories and thresholds live in versioned YAML, and no content is sent to third-party APIs.
3.highlight_1: 0.6 confidence threshold with a manual review route: below it, the email goes to a review queue instead of getting a guessed label.
3.highlight_2: Prompt, category descriptions and thresholds kept in versioned configuration, outside the execution flow: changing behavior doesn't require editing the workflow.
3.highlight_3: Python watchdog triggered by a systemd timer, outside the container, that queries the execution database and alerts when there's no activity within the expected window.
3.challenge_1: Diagnosing a silent failure: the model returned labels outside the expected set without raising any error. I traced the cause to the context window and measured accuracy on a batch of real emails before and after the fix.
3.challenge_2: Making sure an outage can't go unnoticed: a credential expired silently and triage stopped for 38 days without anyone noticing — which led to the out-of-container watchdog.

4.name: Skin Analyser — AI Skin Lesion Triage
4.description: Classification pipeline for dermoscopic images from the public HAM10000 dataset: OpenCV preprocessing, patient-level splits with no data leakage, 8 CNN architectures compared with transfer learning, and evaluation by F1, recall, AUC and confusion matrix. A triage project: it does not diagnose.
4.highlight_1: Train, validation and test sets split by patient_id with class stratification: images from the same patient never land in different partitions.
4.highlight_2: 8 architectures (MobileNetV2, EfficientNetB0, ResNet50, InceptionV3, DenseNet121, Xception, VGG19 and NASNetMobile) compared under an identical protocol, in a parameterized pipeline where only the configuration changes.
4.highlight_3: Runs and metrics persisted in Supabase, with a daily KPI dashboard — accuracy, sensitivity and specificity — built on PostgreSQL materialized views.
4.challenge_1: Designing validation so the numbers mean something: patient-level splits and recall prioritized for the class with the highest clinical risk.
4.challenge_2: Controlling overfitting with augmentation, dropout, L2 regularization, early stopping and learning-rate reduction on plateau, tracking the train/validation gap every epoch.
